themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: This week, curb condition complaints spiked to 7 (211% above the 2.2-complaint weekly average) and damaged street signs jumped to 10 (264% above the 2.8 weekly average), suggesting rapid physical degradation of street infrastructure in Woodhaven/Richmond Hill.
evidence: Curb condition: 7 complaints this week vs. 2.2 weekly average (211% spike, z-score 7.18)
Street sign damage: 10 complaints this week vs. 2.8 weekly average (264% spike, z-score 5.58)
Both spikes occurred in the most recent reporting week, indicating acute acceleration
reporting_angles: Investigate whether recent weather events or deferred maintenance triggered simultaneous curb and signage failures across the district
Interview residents about safety hazards from damaged street infrastructure and track city response times on 311 repairs

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Over the past week, commercial noise complaints spiked to 22 (300% above the 5.5 weekly average), the largest proportional jump in the district's noise category, suggesting a concentrated expansion of disruptive commercial activity.
evidence: Noise - Commercial: 22 complaints this week vs. 5.5 weekly average (300% spike, z-score 4.30)
Commercial noise is now the 8th-ranked complaint type district-wide despite typically being minor
Spike emerged suddenly this week with no corresponding residential noise spike, indicating specific commercial sources
reporting_angles: Identify which commercial establishments or construction projects triggered the complaints and whether they have proper permits
Map complaint locations to determine if the noise is concentrated in one neighborhood zone (e.g., near retail corridor or transit hub)

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Infestation
themes_detail.summary: This week, illegal posting complaints jumped to 8 (357% above the 1.8 weekly average), indicating rapid proliferation of unlicensed advertisements or notices across street infrastructure.
evidence: Illegal Posting: 8 complaints this week vs. 1.8 weekly average (357% spike, z-score 4.49)
Spike is recent and sharp, suggesting new posting campaign or reduced enforcement
Pairs with street sign damage spike, indicating general infrastructure deterioration
reporting_angles: Determine whether the postings are linked to a specific business, event, or organized effort
Check if DSNY enforcement has been reduced in this district and request explanation from the city

themes_detail.label: Plumbing & Water System Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 2 weeks, plumbing complaints spiked to 3 (700% above the 0.4 weekly average), and water system complaints remain elevated at 272 total over 90 days, suggesting emerging building-level water infrastructure failures across the district.
evidence: Plumbing: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Water System: 272 complaints over last 90 days, indicating sustained baseline issue
Heat/Hot Water: 776 complaints over 90 days, 8th-ranked category, suggests related building infrastructure vulnerabilities
reporting_angles: Investigate whether aging water mains or building code violations are causing simultaneous plumbing failures across multiple addresses
Interview residents about water quality, pressure, or heating issues and cross-reference with DOB violation data

themes_detail.label: Parks & Green Space Demand Surge
themes_detail.summary: This week, tree request complaints jumped to 3 (700% above the 0.4 weekly average), aligning with long-standing community board budget requests for park improvements, suggesting residents are increasingly vocal about environmental infrastructure gaps.
evidence: New Tree Request: 3 complaints this week vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Community Board budget data shows repeated, multi-year requests for park improvements and new amenities
Spike is recent and represents convergence of citizen demand and formal budget advocacy
reporting_angles: Profile the tree request complaints to understand which neighborhoods feel under-greened and why
Review community board's multi-year park improvement requests and investigate why they remain unfunded
